target_customer: Cancer centers, oncologists and pharma biomarker teams that order tumor genomic testing
problem: Standard tumor tests read only a panel of known mutations, missing most of the genome. Isabl runs whole genome and transcriptome analysis from one sequencing run.
business_model: Diagnostic test and WGTS SaaS software for labs and pharma partners

founders.name: Elli Papaemmanuil
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch says the company came from her research at MSK; listed as founder on YC page. Education not found.

founders.name: Juan Medina
founders.background_notes: Co-founder and CTO per YC page. TechCrunch calls him Juan Santiago Medina.

founders.name: Andrew Kung
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder by TechCrunch and listed on the YC page. Background not found in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: Whole genome and transcriptome analysis for clinical use requires validated bioinformatics pipelines, sequencing partnerships and regulatory work; the product later received FDA Breakthrough Device Designation per its website.

defensibility.rationale: Clinical validation and FDA designation are slow to replicate, and the technology came from years of incubation at Memorial Sloan Kettering.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source found showing an incumbent copying or buying Isabl.

market_need_then: Panel based tumor tests were standard of care and miss structural variants and non coding changes, while sequencing costs were falling.

branding.domain_note: Uses isabl.io and later isabl.com style pages; history not found.

brand_strength.rationale: Branding search returned only name meanings of the unrelated name Isabel; no press on the brand.

outcome_analysis: Isabl spun out of Memorial Sloan Kettering and joined YC in Winter 2020, then raised a 3 million seed in May 2022 led by Two Sigma Ventures. It remains active with FDA Breakthrough Device Designation claimed on its site. Clinical diagnostics move slowly, so the long gap between batch and seed reflects validation work rather than failure. No acquisition or shutdown found.
notes: CB Insights agrees on 3M seed on 2022-05-18. A grant listing and aggregators mention a 2M NCI SBIR grant and a total up to 5M; date not found so not recorded as a round. Other aggregators list extra investors (Bossa Invest, Sand Hill Angels), unverified. Competitors left empty: Foundation Medicine, Tempus and Caris appear only in undated or later pages, nothing dated near early 2020 was opened.
